title: Etale lifts descend along an extension of a separably closed field
statement: Let f : X -> S be an etale morphism of schemes [def-weil-etale-morphism], L a separably closed field [def-pc-separably-closed], Omega a field, and beta : L -> Omega a field embedding. Let tau : Spec L -> S and g : Spec Omega -> X satisfy g followed by f = Spec(beta) followed by tau. Then there exists gprime : Spec L -> X such that Spec(beta) followed by gprime = g and gprime followed by f = tau.

source.place: Scheme.Hom.exists_SpecMap_comp_eq_of_isSepClosed; proved source-library theorem implementing residue-field descent (Stacks 03QW, paragraph before Theorem 59.56.3)

proof.text: Factor g and tau through the residue fields of their image points using lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-field. The compatibility with f identifies the image of g with the image of tau and gives compatible residue-field embeddings. The residue-field extension induced by the etale f is separable, by lem-weil-pbc-etale-residue-field-extension-separable. Every image element of this separable extension has a separable minimal polynomial. Its image polynomial splits over L, and its root in Omega belongs to the image of beta (Polynomial.Splits.mem_range_of_isRoot). Thus the residue-field embedding into Omega factors through beta; the proved RingHom.exists_comp_eq_of_isSepClosed constructs this factorization as a ring homomorphism. Compose its Spec map with the residue-field inclusion into X to obtain gprime. Residue-field naturality and the factorization identity prove the first equality. Injectivity of beta cancels it in the compatible residue-field diagram, proving the equality over S. This is exactly the complete proof of the existing Scheme.Hom.exists_SpecMap_comp_eq_of_isSepClosed.

lean.statement:
lemma Scheme.Hom.exists_SpecMap_comp_eq_of_isSepClosed (f : X ⟶ S) [Etale f] {L Ω : Type u}
    [Field L] [IsSepClosed L] [Field Ω] (β : CommRingCat.of L ⟶ CommRingCat.of Ω)
    (τ : Spec (.of L) ⟶ S) (g : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ X) (hg : g ≫ f = Spec.map β ≫ τ) :
    ∃ g' : Spec (.of L) ⟶ X, Spec.map β ≫ g' = g ∧ g' ≫ f = τ
